 Wisconsin high school football: Top 10 Level 2 matchups 
 Several rematches this week, including Oconomowoc at defending Division 1 champion Arrowhead and Franklin at Muskego.

By Norbert Durst 
Oct 30, 2026, 8:00am 
 Kingston Allen goes off again! 
 31,934 views 
 1:02 
Level 2 of the Wisconsin high school football playoffs is here and we are putting the spotlight on the biggest games. 
 Full list of NFHS Network streams 
 Level 1 playoff games to watch 
 All listed games are scheduled for Friday at 7 p.m. 
 Oconomowoc  (7-3) at Arrowhead  (9-1) 
 Classic Eight Conference rivals meet again after Arrowhead won the regular-season matchup 35-0. Defending Division 1 state champion Arrowhead, which opened the playoffs with a 37-0 win over Oshkosh West, is led by running backs Jebari Craig and Devin Nettles . Craig has rushed for 1,525 yards and 20 touchdowns, while Nettles has rushed for 1,027 yards and 14 scores. Oconomowoc running back Damian Bartolotta rushed for 205 yards and five touchdowns in last week's 52-35 win over Middleton. Bartolotta has rushed for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns. 
 Hudson (Hudson, Wis.) (9-1) at Verona  (9-1)
 Watch live NFHS Network 
Hudson extended its winning streak to five games with a 38-12 win over Chippewa Falls, while Big Eight Conference champion Verona won its eighth straight with a 24-16 victory over Sun Prairie East. Senior quarterback Grant Bjerke has accounted for 38 touchdowns. He has rushed for 1,543 yards and 27 touchdowns and passed for 1,203 yards and 11 scores. Verona running back Jax Wepking has rushed for 1,112 yards and 13 touchdowns.
 Neenah  (7-3) at Bay Port  (9-1) 
Neenah has rebounded from a 1-3 start with six straight wins, including a 36-21 victory over De Pere last week. Quarterback Ashton VanBeek , a North Dakota State commit at linebacker, has passed for 1,113 yards and 12 touchdowns and rushed for 867 yards and 17 scores. Bay Port opened its bid for a third consecutive appearance in the Division 1 state championship game with a 32-7 win over Wausau West. Quarterback Bray Babich has passed for 1,418 yards and 15 touchdowns and rushed for five more scores.
 Franklin  (6-4) at Muskego  (9-1) 
Muskego opened with a 63-0 win over Milwaukee Hamilton/Audubon. The Warriors are led offensively by running back Bryson Hoeffler , who has 994 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns, and their defense has allowed just 75 points this season. Franklin gets another shot at Muskego after losing their regular-season meeting 31-6. The Sabers advanced with a 16-6 victory over Kenosha Bradford. Quarterback Keegan Best has passed for 1,616 yards and 14 touchdowns for the Sabers. 
 Marquette University  (7-3) at Hamilton  (10-0) 
Hamilton looks to beat Marquette for the second time in three weeks after winning the regular-season finale 42-20. The unbeaten Chargers followed with a 40-0 victory over Janesville Parker. Quarterback Cole Erdmann directs Hamilton's offense which averages 42.8 points per game. He has passed for 2,129 yards and 24 touchdowns and has 454 rushing yards and seven scores. Running back Brayden Schroeder leads the Chargers' rushing attack with 994 yards and 17 touchdowns. Marquette advanced with a 44-7 win over Madison Memorial. The Hilltoppers are led by quarterback Ben Schroeder and running back Bear Bonk . Schroeder has passed for 2,157 yards and 21 touchdowns, while Bonk has rushed for 1,395 yards and 20 scores. 
 Aquinas  (9-1) at West Salem  (10-0) 
 Coulee Conference rivals meet again after West Salem handed Aquinas its only loss, 35-6, on Sept. 4. The Panthers opened the playoffs with a 55-6 win over Wisconsin Dells, while the Blugolds defeated Xavier 30-6. Quarterback Drew McConkey has accounted for 27 touchdowns, passing for 961 yards and 10 touchdowns and rushing for 1,018 yards and 17 scores. Aquinas is paced by quarterback Owen Ludlow , who has passed for 1,449 yards and 15 touchdowns. 
 Wisconsin commit Kingston Allen, the nation’s leader in rushing yards and total touchdowns, is 788 yards shy of the state career rushing record. (FILE PHOTO: Owen Laack) 
 Menasha  (8-2) at Notre Dame Academy  (10-0) 
Wisconsin commit Kingston Allen set another state record last week, scoring six touchdowns in Notre Dame’s 63-9 win over Germantown to reach 116 total touchdowns for his career. Allen is now within 800 rushing yards of the state career record of 7,416, set by Colton Brunell of Columbus. He leads the nation with 2,797 rushing yards and 54 rushing touchdowns this season. Menasha advanced with a 43-22 win over Menomonee Falls but faces a difficult rematch after a 66-18 regular-season loss to the Tritons.
 West Bend West  (8-2) at Homestead  (9-1)
 Watch live NFHS Network 
 Homestead advanced with a 57-20 win over Burlington. The Highlanders average 40.6 points per game and are led by running back Vincent Yodbut , who has rushed for 1,347 yards and 19 touchdowns. Quarterback Lee Zortman ranks second on the team with 703 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns. West Bend West earned its first playoff win in program history with a 38-6 victory over Slinger. Quarterback Collin Grass has passed for 837 yards and 11 touchdowns and ranks second on the team with 10 rushing touchdowns.
 Lodi  (7-3) at Little Chute  (9-1)
 Watch live NFHS Network 
 Little Chute, which played in last year's Division 4 state championship game, opened the playoffs with a 51-10 win over Denmark and has scored at least 49 points in four straight games. The Mustangs feature a run-heavy offense led by running back Reece Joten (947 rushing yards, 11 touchdowns) and quarterback Jaden Hermsen (553 rushing yards, 12 touchdowns). Hermsen also has six touchdown passes. Lodi advanced with a 49-12 win over Mauston and features quarterback Kale Schneider , who has passed for 1,829 yards and 18 touchdowns and rushed for 485 yards and 10 scores. 
 Cuba City  (7-3) at St. Joseph  (8-2)
 Watch live NFHS Network   
Last year's Division 7 state champion St. Joseph, now in Division 6, opened the playoffs with a 49-0 win over Poynette. Quarterback Christopher Kenesie has passed for 865 yards and 11 touchdowns and rushed for 849 yards and 14 scores. He also leads the team with 78 tackles and four interceptions. Cuba City advanced with a 27-9 win over Benton/Scales Mound/Shullsburg and is led by running back Bradley Rowe , who has 1,024 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns and ranks second on the team in tackles.
